Check a results object against the contract

Source: R/check_results.R
check_results.Rd

check_results() checks a results object against the contract of save_results(). It reports each rule as PASS or FAIL, and it stops on nothing.

Usage

check_results(x)

Arguments

x

The results object, normally from read_results().

Value

A data.frame with one row per rule and the columns rule, status and detail. status is "PASS" or "FAIL".

Details

The six rules:

  • top_level_names: the names are manifest, exclusions, estimates, tables and extra, each once, and there are no others.

  • exclusions_table: exclusions is a data.frame with the columns step, n_before, n_excluded and n_after. When manifest$stacked is TRUE, it also has the column sim that run_scenarios() adds. On every row, n_before - n_excluded == n_after.

  • no_fitted_models: no element anywhere in x inherits from lm, glm, gam, merMod, brmsfit, coxph or lavaan.

  • no_row_per_person: no data.frame anywhere in x has manifest$n_rows_data rows. When n_rows_data is NA, this rule checks nothing.

  • manifest_scenario: manifest has the elements scenario, sim and sims, and scenario is one string.

  • manifest_data: manifest has exactly one of data_md5 and fake_md5. It has data_md5 when scenario is "real", and fake_md5 when scenario is another string. fake_md5 MUST be one string of 32 lower-case hex digits. data_md5 MUST be a character vector of such strings, named by file. It has length 0 when the data folder has no file. A results file that pbn 2026.11.18 or older wrote has data_md5 for a fake scenario, so it fails this rule.

See also

Other results: read_results(), save_results()

Examples

x <- list(
  manifest = list(
    scenario = "real",
    sim = 1L,
    sims = 1L,
    data_md5 = c(d.csv = "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef"),
    n_rows_data = 100L
  ),
  exclusions = data.frame(
    step = "age 18 or more",
    n_before = 100,
    n_excluded = 4,
    n_after = 97
  ),
  estimates = data.frame(term = "x", estimate = 1.2),
  tables = list(),
  extra = list()
)
pbn::check_results(x)
#>                rule status
#> 1   top_level_names   PASS
#> 2  exclusions_table   FAIL
#> 3  no_fitted_models   PASS
#> 4 no_row_per_person   PASS
#> 5 manifest_scenario   PASS
#> 6     manifest_data   PASS
#>                                                                 detail
#> 1                              the five top-level names, and no others
#> 2                    n_before - n_excluded != n_after on these rows: 1
#> 3                                        no fitted model in the object
#> 4                                           no data.frame has 100 rows
#> 5  the manifest names the scenario, the simulation and the simulations
#> 6 the manifest has data_md5 for "real" or fake_md5 for a fake scenario
